title: Characterization of Ferroelectric Oxide-based Devices with Large Pockels Effect Using Advanced STEM
content: Electro-optical (EO) modulator is significant in the development of high-speed, low-power computation. BaTiO3 (BTO) is a well-known ferroelectric oxide and has been widely applied across fields, such as ferroelectric random-access memory, electro-caloric coolers, etc [1]. Over the past few years, a large Pockels effect has been demonstrated in a Si-integrated BTO-based EO modular. The Pockels coefficient of BTO is ∼ 1300 pm/V in bulk form [2], and ∼ 923 pm/V and in thin film [3], which is much larger than that of other typical ferroelectrics (LiNbO3, ∼ 30 pm/V) [4]. However, there are abundant non-ideal microstructural features in BTO, especially the domain configurations, with the effect on Pockels effect remaining elusive. Furthermore, the Pockels effect is dependent upon the phonon modes [5,6], in which the contribution from distinct phonon modes is also unclear in BTO. In this work, we utilized different cooling rate to modify the domain configurations in BTO and employed advanced scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM and momentum-resolved STEM-EELS) to identify the domain configurations in BTO and its accompanied phonon mode.
